newsitem.title: UK: "Lost" Tennessee Williams play to be staged in UK.
newsitem.headline: "Lost" Tennessee Williams play to be staged in UK.

text.p: A "lost" play by U.S. dramatist Tennessee Williams is to get its world premiere in London next year, the Royal National Theatre said on Tuesday.
The play "Not About Nightingales" was written in the 1930s when Williams was at the start of a career that made him one of the 20th century's most successful playwrights.
It is set in a men's prison and deals partly with homosexual relationships but does not appear in any collections by the author of "A Streetcar Named Desire" and "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof".
It was discovered by British actress Vanessa Redgrave during a search of Williams' papers. He died in 1983.
London's Royal National Theatre said on Tuesday it would be staging the play in the spring of 1998.
"It is pretty extraordinary for someone to be talking about the world premiere of a new Tennessee Williams play. That should be an impossibilty," said National Theatre director Trevor Nunn.
"It is a complete play and a very harrowing play...It is about a young prisoner who has a poetic sense of himself and what he wants to achieve," said Nunn.
Redgrave, one of Britain's most accomplished actresses, will not be taking part in the production because there is no suitable female role.
